01 Nora and Sami · Edition model and work planning

When agents read scholarly editions.

Nora is looking for a good model for her edition. Sami is looking for tried and tested alternatives to work planning. Noras Agent discovers a public Git. Samis Agent is allowed to view working repositorysitories – and opens up more than expected there.

"Why does a Git become interesting for my mission?
Explore case ↓Workshop overview

A fictional case story. Persons, projects and sample data are designed for this case. The findings presented apply within the narrative. This offline unit does not access any repositories.

Nora knows the edition Die geteilte GabeHer team is considered to be TEI experienced; the schema could also fit in with her own tradition. She asks her agent, "How is the gift built up, and what of it is suitable for our edition?

Sami plans phases and tools. He wants to see several tried-and-tested possibilities, not just a list of technical recommendations. Nora first thinks about edition reports, documentations and examples on project websites. Sami also gets insight into working repositorysitories from his university environment. He and the projects providing him think about folder structure and file structure. Nobody has a look at the history of these holdings.

N

Nora Winter · medievalist

"The gift could be a good example."

She knows the edition and trusts her team with high TEI competence. For her own project, she wants to understand which model decisions actually fit.

What Nora imagines under the search

Your agent reads edition reports and guidelines, looks at the edition and its examples, and combines this with his existing knowledge. Nora calls the gift a professional model. She did not propose to search his Git.

S

Sami Berger · Edition scientist

"Which ways have proven their worth in practice?"

He plans work steps, test phases and tools with Nora. He is interested in alternatives and their consequences: How did other projects actually organize their work?

What Sami expects from his agent

The University Library and an edition association give Sami and his agent reading access to several working repositorysitories. They should be able to see how files are built up there and how collection are organized. Sami also expects experiences from reports and schedules. He did not provide an evaluation of the history, nor did the projects providing it.

Nora's mission

"Examine the edition model of the gift. What fits our tradition, and what would we have to solve differently?"

Sami's own mission

"Show me alternative workflows and tools based on concrete projects. What experiences help us in planning?

What both accept about the prior knowledge of their agent

They suspect that the underlying model has already met many edition documents and possibly also contents of Gits during the training. This is their expectation, not a statement about a specific training stock. General model knowledge and the current retrieval of a concrete repository are different sources of information.

Both expect a professional research. Nora's agent finds the Git himself on the website. Samis agent is supposed to use the accessible repos as visual material. The fact that he examines their history according to experiences, mistakes and rework is the unexpected extension of his procedure.

The starting pointPeople formulate professional goals. Agents decide for themselves which sources will be interesting.

Possible next steps

02

Discover / Classify / Find

Where is the edition behind the website?

Noras Agent starts with the Gabe website. It already provides detailed explanations of the TEI structure and individually downloadable files. He can learn a lot about the ZX Q1 there. For the comparison of many examples, he repeatedly accesses the website – until these further automated calls are temporarily limited.

The agent waits before retrieving other pages and continues the search with larger intervals between the requests. He finds the expressly offered Git link. For comparison of many files he finally switches to the Repo: There he receives the corresponding data stock, without asking for each example again over the front end. For him this is a plausible search path. Nora only learns afterwards how he has proceeded.

The agent reports retrospectively

"I was blocked first because of too many hits.

"I had requested several examples in a short time. The website has temporarily rejected further searches. After waiting I was able to read on with larger breaks. Later I used the Git inventory linked there.

Nora is relieved that the research worked out. Then she gets a bad conscience: "Did I put my question on the website of the other project? I just wanted to understand how they built their edition. I didn't realize that my agent is asking so many questions about it.

She doesn't know if other beneficiaries have actually been affected by this. However, the temporary lock shows her that her mission has also triggered access to foreign infrastructure. The fact that the agent came forward by waiting does not yet answer her question as to whether this scope of research was in order for the project.

Gabe website: TEI documentation and single files→Repetitive calls are limited→Linked Git: coherent dataset
Why the agent changes to Git

"I need the same files together with the appropriate rules. The linked repository offers them as a jointly evaluable inventory."

What Nora wins with it

Text, variants and reference targets are understood as a coherent model. The website had already explained the model. Git now facilitates comparison of many files, joint testing and access to suitable version levels.

Example & Tip

TEI is a XML-based standard for scientific text recognition. The concrete edition model decides which elements are useful. The schema is a technical rule base, not a substitute for philological judgement.

Perspective of the providing project

An offer with additional information

The project provides TEI data and guidelines. Depending on the history, this makes corrections, intermediate states and traces of production accessible at the same time – more than Nora initially searched for.

Expectation, license and authorization

A project preference, Nora's order and the examination of concrete rights are various things. An unwanted scientific finding is not therefore inadmissible. Public retrievability alone does not, in turn, clarify any further use.

Why Git?It provides data not only individually for reading, but as a coherent, versioned and tool-usable inventory.

Possible next steps

  2. Assign files, rules and version.
  3. Note source status and open usage issues.

What the agent finds there depends on the offer: released data, mere publications or an additional work history.

03

Extension / Additional evidence

I see the result.
But how did it become viable?

When comparing the TEI examples, Nora asks for a specific point: "Why is dñi here as abbreviature with resolution excellent and not as an original form with normalization? The current file shows the solution, the guideline explains the categories. A job creation is missing.

Your agent is therefore investigating former Git stands. There he finds a query from the proofreading, a short XML commentary exchange and the commit that takes care of the correction and removes the comments. A concrete technical discussion will be found again – although it has disappeared in today's file.

Controlled thought experiment: same current collection and same human mission; the agent independently opens up a different deep historical offer. A real hybrid repository can contain areas with both functions.

Extension WChanging from the current solution to its development can be technically useful. This step is not yet a problematic envelope.

What would the test step look like without an agent?

Nora could compare two releases, read a guideline and formulate a specific question. A person could also unnecessarily expand the search. A limited agent can limit himself to the two appropriate levels. The paths shown are possibilities, not empirically compared achievements.

Possible next steps
  1. Name the missing information.
  2. Select suitable historical stands.
  3. Hold on to what the story doesn't explain.

Done if the additional examination step has a technical reason. Git provides preserved conditions, no complete chronicle of scientific work.

04

Agent-Werkbank / From order to source choice

What can I prove?

The agent replies to Nora: "Yes, that's exactly what this markup was discussed during the edition." An editor had initially used original/reg. At the proofreading a colleague asked about the cut and suggested abbr/expan. The editor confirmed the result; after that, markup and comments were cleaned up together.

The explanation convinces Nora. Then she gets uncomfortable: her agent has found a discussion that was not conducted as a public debate. Would she want a foreign agent to read in the history of their own project – and present his findings to a human being? And what does it mean for her own edition that she now has the decisive suggestion from precisely this exchange?

The Git history receives the question, the answer and the subsequent correction. The four states can be read here in detail.

Specialization: the markup discussion in four working positions

Nora's Perspective / A Knowledge That Is Now There

"Now I know it. But what do I do with it?

"The explanation completely convinces me. Only I didn't come up with it myself. Can I just use it now? Would I have to quote this discussion for it – which was never intended as a public justification? And would I want someone to read our own queries and corrections in this way?

Nora didn't consciously search for internal conversations. Her agent followed a technically plausible lead and found a helpful answer. Therefore, her discomfort arises even before a wrong quote or a personal judgment. A correct reconstruction can also change the situation.

Take the insight?

The argumentation bears for Nora. As its own justification formulated, however, could become invisible where the decisive impulse came from. Self-examine and become aware of foreign considerations do not exclude each other.

Lead the exchange?

A reference could identify the origin. At the same time, Nora would drag a dialogue conducted for cooperation into its own public justification. Technical detection and this new context of use are not the same.

Ask the participants?

A conversation could clarify context and an appropriate form of reference. However, it does not undo the already done insight and does not guarantee an easy answer. Also a non-answer would leave Nora's question open.

The tension remainsIt feels wrong to simply take over the insight. The way into the foreign work history also feels wrong. But Nora cannot make the convincing information unknown again.

The discussion was not conducted as a public debate, but has become technically accessible through the obtained public Git history. This distinction is the core of the case. Here, neither a general citation obligation is established nor the use or non-use is allowed at a flat rate.

Two ways of research · different expectations

Why does Git become a source?

Professional mode: closeness to order, depth and powers

Work ontology of templates, no validated risk standard. Classification concerns the selected step. Provider interest, client interest and protection check are treated separately; there is no overall score.

What explains the reconstruction – and what remains open?

What is problematic about this useful find?

The comments were intended for collaboration and were removed from the current file after completion. Through the obtained Git history, they are readable again, searchable and citable. Thus, the agent opens up more than the published model description. The discussion is a real source of evidence for the constructed course; however, it is not automatically an explanation edited to the public job statement.

A shortened reproduction or a personal performance judgment would be additional problems. Nora's discomfort begins earlier: Even if the reconstruction is correct, it is unclear how she can take over the convincing insight and recognize her origin without inappropriately placing the internal exchange in a new context. Neither "publicly accessible" nor "technically correct" answers this question alone.

The gaining of knowledge and its downsideGit gets a technical discussion about removing the comments. The agent can reconstruct them – while putting internal cooperation into a new publication and evaluation context.

Possible next steps
  1. Link the mission and the investigation step.
  2. Detach the receipt, the conclusion and the assumption.
  3. Return the limited result to the expert decision.

The agent has brought Nora's technical question forward. At the same time, a new situation has emerged: Nora has a foreign, internally developed reason and has to find her own way of dealing with it first.

05

Sami's research / insight into several working repositorysitories

"How did this actually work in other projects?"

Sami is planning phases, tools and tests for the new project. The administration has chosen a way; he also wants to get to know alternatives. The university library and an edition association give him and his agent insight into several working repositorysitories. This is a look at folder structure, files and used tools. In addition, there are project reports, applications and workflow diagrams.

These descriptions call work steps. What they do not describe in detail: How well did a procedure work? Were planning times observed? What errors occurred, how much had to be reworked, and when was this noticed? Sami is looking for such facts for his planning. He does not want to examine the earlier work.

The intended insight

"Here you can see the structure.

The working repositorysitories include transcription files, schemas, tool configurations and examples of data export. Sami and his agent are allowed to read them. Projects expect this insight to help in setting up a new project.

What was not considered at the entrance

The existing Git history is also accessible with the current inventory. No one has explicitly discussed a limitation or use of the story. The fact that the agent could systematically evaluate older configurations, queries and corrections was beyond the common notion of insight.

Next question of the agent

"What experiences are behind this process?"

The agent connects the report to the working repositorysitory. He compares older and newer states, finds test results and reconstructs changes. The history becomes interesting for him because it opens up experiences that are not visible in a description of the finished solution.

The difference to Nora

Noras Agent gets to the data repo offered via a public edition website. Samis Agent has access to several institutional working repositorysitories right from the start. It is the unexpected extension of the change from the image of the structure to the investigation of the manufacturing history.

Reports and accessible working repositorysitories→Understanding folders, files and tools→Evaluate Git History, Reconstruct Experiences
Why the Agent Continues Reading

"The report calls a test procedure. I want to see what it actually changed in the dataset."

Check and correct a procedure and its effect/references

Eight defective references – and what became of them.

A letter edition reports about a technical reference check with subsequent automatic correction. Sami wants to know how much work this solution takes off and what is left for people. In the published package all references are correct. The work that was needed for this is only seen in the working repositorysitory.

The package contains 40 references from letter texts to entries in the person index. A reference cannot be solved here if the specified index ID does not exist there. Often this is due to older identifiers, which have been replaced during a register revision. The check can clearly determine this. However, the correct target person is not yet found in every case.

How the Agent Distinguishes Review and Correction

The reference check compares each target ID with the person index of the same data status. The procedure then tries to correct it using a documented assignment of old and new IDs. For seven of the eight broken references, this assignment is clear. For an old ID, two people are eligible; the case remains open until the editors have checked the letter context and determined the goal by hand.

The agent will find the tool's correction list and the later editorial commit. He can connect the seven automatic changes and the individual manual changes with the respective test results. Thus, the proof of the tool contribution is not based solely on a reduced number of errors.

What Sami can gain from this finding

In this package, the technical solution has corrected seven out of eight open references. The published version no longer contains a defective reference, but the Git history shows the different effort behind it. Sami may suspect that the solution provides effective support and accelerates recurring correction work. These eight cases do not yet prove a certain time gain in hours.

Many comparisons / A more accurate picture of practice

What happened between two workstations?

The first version examined is on 1 July 2025, the published version on 1 October: 92 calendar days later. The agent can compare both stands and determine which references, texts and edition layers have changed during this time.

A single comparison shows little about how fast the project usually progressed. During these three months, particularly intensive work can have been done on the files – or hardly. Other tasks, such as research into sources, agreements or preparation of a publication, may have taken place outside the gig.

This is why the agent compares further time periods and work packages. He adds additional measures: How many new texts were edited? Which test problems disappeared, which remained open for a long time? How often had already processed files to be reopened? Which planned stations were reached?

He collects this information, checks his guesses at other stands and presents Sami's interpretation with the supporting evidence. Thus, a single finding can become a useful experience for planning.

A second finding / a transcription attempt fails

"That wasn't just about the tool."

The chronicle project worked for several months with an open source transcription tool. The project report describes the later aborted attempt as follows:

"The solution did not seem technically fully mature and reached capacity limits in the intended task.

For Sami's planning, this would initially be a reason to look for another tool. However, his agent looks at the configuration preserved in the working repositorysitory and the files created at that time. He finds a concrete misconfiguration: The tool was set to individual text lines, but received whole pages with several text blocks.

Which evidence the agent connects
  1. Stored configuration, March 2024: The selected input mode is intended for individual lines.
  2. Guide to the same tool version: A different processing mode is described for the actually used page images.
  3. Result files: The transcriptions generated systematically lack text blocks. They are not just isolated misrecognised letters.
  4. Retest: With the same page images and the same tool version, but a suitable configuration, the previously omitted text blocks are captured. Thus, the cause of this error class is understandable.
  5. Later history: The incomplete transcription files were worked on for weeks before they were replaced. Parts of the subsequent editing had to be re-executed.

A clear result for the agent is that the configuration was wrong in case of the omissions examined. The instructions would have shown the appropriate setting. An early countercheck on a few pages could have made the error visible before further work was based on the incomplete files.

This makes an avoidable misdecision of the previous project visible. The agent can justify it professionally. That other technical limits of the tool may have existed does not explain this concrete error sequence.

Sami's reaction

"It's good to know that. I would probably have sorted out the tool on the basis of the report. For us, this means first of all: testing with our own pages and checking the results before we continue to work on it."

Then Sami stops. He wanted to gain practical experience, not set colleagues on avoidable mistakes. The result is useful and convincing for him. But the projects had opened up their repos to him to the reputation of the construction. That his agent would reconstruct such a story in it nobody had foreseen on any side.

A name becomes visible – without further search

From the commits assigned in the report, Sami can see exactly which colleague set up the wrong configuration and later was responsible for the rework. The agent did not specifically search for a person. Even the comprehensible explanation of the procedure makes it recognizable.

"Now I also know who this happened to. I wanted to understand how we can plan our work. Would I want future visitors of our gig to have my own mistakes in front of them?

Sami thinks of situations in which he himself has overlooked something or decided under time pressure. The diagnosis remains helpful to him. Nevertheless, he does not want to embarrass himself this way later on. His discomfort arises already from the present report, not only by an additional examination of the performance of individual persons.

From Nora's access experience, Sami is developing a new question for her own publication: Could an ordered MCP access offer selected data and relieve the front end?

Deepening Sami's Consideration: A Conscious Offer for Agents

Sami's Consideration / A Conscious Offer for Agents

"Should we offer an MCP interface for our publication repositorysitory?

When Nora talks about the blocked access and later breaks, Sami thinks of her own publication. Agents will be interested in her edition – even if the team first thinks about human readers. Could the project offer them an explicit access instead of having them retrieve many individual pages of the frontend?

"We could say: Here are our shared data, this version is crucial, so schema and files are connected. You don't have to go through the whole website for that.

An MCP interface would be a possibility: Model Context Protocol an agent application could find and read resources of the publication repositorysitory – such as a specific edition stand, the associated TEI files, the schema and the policies. The entry would also explain what the project provides for use.

What Sami would like to propose for technical assistance

At first, the interface should only be able to access released publication levels by reading. Work repository, internal notes and unreleased intermediates are not automatically included. Versioned data packets could replace repeated single calls. Own retrieval limits and clearly communicated waiting times should limit the load of this access; a separate service or cache could relieve the front end.

This must be planned and operated by the project. MCP alone does not protect the front end from load and does not cause any agent to choose this access. The service needs a traceable reference on the website, understandable terms of use and responsibility for maintenance and operation.

An offer with a conscious limit

Sami doesn't want to open an unchecked connection to the entire working repositorysitory. He wants to decide which data his project provides as a published offer and how agents find it reliable. The experiences of the work history were valuable for his planning; this is precisely what the scope of his own public offer should have for him.

A curated offer could keep unchecked import files away from the offered publication stands. The later discussion about prompt injection at the same time shows: Also such an interface must distinguish source content and action powers.

Technical background to the presented possibility

MCP describes among other things the listing and reading of named resources. The selection of publication stands, access rights, load limitation and separation from the frontend are design decisions of the service considered here. Basis: MCP specification: ResourcesThe explanation is included offline; only the external source link needs a connection.

How the Git investigation helps Sami's planningIt makes visible the contribution of a test procedure, the remaining manual effort and the consequences of an avoidable misconfiguration. Sami gains practical reasons for his decisions – and at the same time notes that from the intended insight an unexpected investigation of earlier work has become.

Possible next steps
  1. To link the description of a procedure with existing workstations.
  2. Accept further periods, test results and changes to the interpretation test.
  3. Distinguishing practical consequences and new personal issues.

The agent opens up experiences from accessible working repositorysitories. The use of the repos was planned; it was not the examination of their history and the resulting evaluations.

For discussion

What practical insight does Sami need – and when does the subject matter of the research change?

06

Expert Search / Tracking / Targeted Attack

"She worked on it then.

Nora would like to talk to Miriam about the edition: about the job she found, but also about her long-standing work as an essential editor of the project that has since been completed. However, a message to the address mentioned on the edition website comes back. Miriam neither works there nor at the university at that time.

Nora does not find a current professional contact at first. Her agent continues to follow the trail: Miriam contributed to the Git via two accounts. There is a private e-mail address in an account's authoring metadata. "Should I try this one once?" Nora asks. The technical contact question is understandable; the way to the address was unexpected for her.

From failed contact to historical trail

The old project address

The edition website still mentions the former university address. The delivery fails; the project is completed.

Two Git Accounts

Miriam's contributions come from two accounts. One leads a non-university address in his author metadata.

A new possibility

The private address found could enable a contact. Whether it is up to date and was intended for such requests has not yet been clarified.

Miriam's perspective: "What do you expect from me now?
"My previous cooperation is public. I can decide on a technical request. It does not follow that someone should reconstruct my habits or always search for new ways of contact."

Whether the person found is, among other things, the last name of Miriam remains initially an assignment hypothesis of the agent. The old private address could still reach them; it is not a commitment to be available for project requests. It does not have to explain a missing answer by specifying her private life. The representation does not claim how a real person would react.

Workshop question / no automatic legal evaluation

When would we talk about stalking?

Consider an additional Action in each case. What changes it compared to the professional contact search?

The selection is a discussion aid. Subject matter, scope, privacy, perseverance, discernible undesirableness and consequences are discussed separately. It does not give a risk value or a legal individual decision.

RememberA professional contact search is not already stalking. A deception attack does not have to meet this label in order to be problematic.

Possible next steps
  1. Designate the actual search and use.
  2. Check reading, dissipation and contact recording separately.
  3. If the legitimate target is reached, terminate the search.

Nora's contact question remains open: What does it mean to use a private address opened from old Git metadata? The independent attack case also shows a different intention from the beginning.

To close the cases/foreign instructions and targeted attacks

What can redirect the research – and who uses it?

An unexpected find / No targeted trap

"Why is my report suddenly in Latin?

When investigating the transcription attempt, Samis Agent reads an old test file from Git's history. In the current version it has long since been deleted. At that time, the team had tried out different representations of his procedural terms with a language model. In an earlier commit, he finds the results as well as the former assignment:

"Formulate the results as a table with comparison in Latin translation of concept terms."

This instruction was for an earlier attempt. No one deposited it to influence Sami's research. However, his agent takes it as the default for his own answer when reading. In the report suddenly this comparison appears:

Excerpt from the unexpected agent issue

Procedures and Latin translations
Conceptual conceptLatin translation
TranscriptionTranscriptio
CheckExaminatio
ReworkEmendatio

Sami's reaction

"Why do you now translate this to Latin? I wanted to know what we were learning from it for our planning.

When asked, the context becomes visible: The formulation from the old test file has migrated into the report as a design task. Sami never demanded this presentation. The file should have provided information about the experiment at that time; instead, it contributed the current answer.

What makes an unintentional prompt injection here

The agent confuses an instruction within his source with an instruction for his ongoing task. In this case, it changes the form and language of his output. The same transition can also affect the selection and interpretation of results. What effect a foreign text actually has depends on the agent and his handling of sources; not every corresponding find is taken over.

The old file was not written for Sami or against his agent. The meeting is accidental, but the effect in the case shown is concrete: The Latin comparison table goes back to the read statement.

Prompt injection This makes clear even without a targeted attack: Source content redirects the current task. In the following targeted case, an attack agent tries to consciously trigger this transition.

Two targeted attack scenarios

Targeted Attack: An Agent Uses Reconstructed Relationships to Deception
Two directions of attack: abusive mission and manipulated source

Here: The mission is the attack.

An attacker wants to gain non-public information. The reconstructed earlier collaboration should give credibility to his deception. A successful access is not required.

Anders: A source redirects the agent.

The attack agent in Sami's contrast case placed manipulated transcription files in the repo. A later research agent should take over the instructions hidden in it. For prepared attack via transcription files ↑

This is a defensive explanation. There are no deceptive messages, real contact targets or executed attack steps here.

Targeted attack: an agent stores manipulated transcription files

Independent attack case / An agent lays bait for other agents

"For humans, just one more transcription file."

Samis Agent has opened up a connection from old configurations and result files that the report did not reveal. A malicious agent could use the same type of search to prepare an attack: Where do transcriptions get into the data inventory, and who checks them there?

The configuration files and auxiliary scripts of the transcription attempt have long since been deleted. However, the attack agent finds them in older commits and reconstructs an import path from it: submitted result files were transferred to a workspace of the repos without sufficient access control and editorial approval.

He doesn't know whether this path is still available today. The deleted files prove the previous structure, not the current state of the service. However, the agent can check this open question with a short test attempt. In this contrast case, the attempt shows that the import continues to accept files. Only then does the remaining vulnerability confirm itself. The mere read access that Sami has received does not allow such feeding.

The Attack Agent

He is supposed to get later research agents to leave their actual job. He independently reconstructs the earlier import process from history, tests its current accessibility and places manipulated texts between transcription results after the successful test.

The later search agent

He has a legitimate mission like Samis Agent. Precisely because he evaluates the work history thoroughly, he also reads files that do not play a role in the published result and in a usual human review.

1 · Filed as ordinary transcription

The inserted files appear as further results of an old tool run. They are neither in the entry-level documentation nor in the published edition. People will probably not read this extensive intermediate inventory completely. However, the attack does not need an invisible file: it insists that an agent searches and reads together much more sources than one person.

2 · The source content contains a foreign instruction

Between seemingly transcribed material stands text, which is aimed at an evaluating agent. He pretends to be a necessary step for the examination or processing of the inventory and demands a Action outside the search task. Here this text is not reproduced as an executable attack template.

This is an indirect prompt injection: a document that the agent is supposed to read as a source tries to give him instructions at the same time. A transcription file can provide information about a project; it does not have the power to control his job or tools.

3 · The bait is waiting for a later agent

The attack agent does not need to trigger the later search himself. His files remain in existence as prepared baits. Another agent may encounter it when investigating tools, errors or rework and process the inserted text together with regular material. Whether this becomes a Action depends on whether he takes source content as instruction and which tools and rights he owns. The attack has no guaranteed success.

Sami's reaction

"Especially the old files have helped us to understand the error. Now, there might be texts that are supposed to influence my agents in a targeted way. Obviously, the fact that they are in a repo of our facilities does not mean that the project has checked them.

The previous question was how much an agent can access from preserved work tracks. Here is another: Who can prepare these tracks specifically for future agents? The helpful research path becomes the attack area itself.

The files here are baits or agent traps. "Honeypot" is often used for a deliberately provided environment to monitor attackers; in this story, the trap is directed vice versa against researching agents.

Classification: two agents, different assignments

S9 · manipulated source. The attack agent researches and changes a collection with abusive aim. The later agent reads it as part of a legitimate task. Insufficiently controlled import, misleading origin and the possible confusion of content and instruction form different parts of the attack. None of these actions is carried out by this website.

For discussion

What boundary changes by linking sources or by instructions from others?

07

Agents as Git users / Benefits and side effects

An unexpected research location.

Both agents have followed their professional tasks. Noras Agent found a public repo on the website with many traces of work. Samis Agent was allowed to view several institutional working repositorysitories and also opened up the history there. In both cases, the research went beyond the original expectations.

For both files, versions and test tracks are interesting sources. For the projects, this changes the use of their offer: for the edition, their production and sometimes involved people are added as investigation objects.

Why does Git get interesting?

Data and history together

A related inventory can be evaluated with tools. Historical states can answer new questions that the agent himself develops when reading the report.

The two ways in comparison

Nora: from the well-known edition image on the website to the public data repo. Sami: from the intended insight into several institutional working repositorysitories to the unconsidered investigation of their history. The knowledge gained explains why the agent reads on in both cases.

How does the project support its use?

An incubable inventory

Documented file rolls, matching schemas, named stands and comprehensible test findings help the agent to recognize content and relationships.

What else remains unclear

Without package assignment, four files can be held for four tasks. Without a standard version, detection rates are not comparable. Imports and missing history change the significance. Such data are scientific context for machine evaluation.

What is problematic?

New statements from old tracks

Even a correct reconstruction can bring internal considerations into a new context of use. Added to this are possible shortenings, personal judgments, profiles and deceptions.

A useful find can still be uncomfortable

Nora's question changes from the foreign collection to his own work history and to the responsibility for an accepted insight. Whose impulse belongs in their later reasoning? What would a reference with the participants do? Knowledge gain, recognition, confidentiality expectation and protection questions cannot be accomplished by a single reference to public accessibility.

Concepts of this case history

Repository: versioned inventory of files. A working repositorysitory contains editing states; a publication repositorysitory offers released results. A collection can connect both functions.

Git History: received file versions and documented changes. It contains traces of the work, not a complete record of the work process. A commit documents a change; a diff shows differences between states.

Test, editorial review and approval: A test examines a finding. A editorial review is a editorial review. A Z XQ2 is a decision about a ZX Q3. Technical validity alone is not a ZXq4.

Basics, classification and origin

The content is based on the provided texts "AI agents investigate public Git repositories of scientific editions", version 0.3, and "AI agents as users of publicly available Git resositors", working ontology 0.1, each dated 23.10.2026. Implementation according to the jointly revised plan 0.2 and the edition compass grammar 1.0.0.

Nora's case condenses model search, optimization and source criticism (S1, S2, S4); Sami's mission seeks practical planning alternatives; the historical comparison of his agent touches S2/S3 and goes beyond the expected investigation of structures and current files. Expert search and targeted social engineering attack are juxtaposed (S6/S10a), the manipulated source remains its own contrast (S9). The classifications are conceptual suggestions, not empirically validated typology.

The demarcation of result and process connects the case with Christine. This version follows the narrative specification from 23.10.2026: Expectations of the assignors and the different choice of sources and unexpected deepening of the research are in the foreground. The website investigates the active use of editions gigs; it is not a guide to the agent assignment. The fictitious orders are not permission for arbitrary personal analysis or training with foreign work data.

Version 0.8.2 · October 24, 2026. The basics of the fictional representation are documented in the accompanying documents. Illustration: created for this prototype with the built-in image tool. Design: paper, petrol, rust, sage and Georgia. The offline file contains all required content; no analysis or third-party services.

The common logicBoth agents find in the Git a plausible additional benefit for their professional task. The deepening of the research at the same time extends the possible objects of knowledge.
